name: Multiple myeloma / plasma cell neoplasms
theme: the marathon · ranked only on what has finished aging

meta.title: Multiple myeloma in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Multiple myeloma spectrum (MGUS -> high-risk smoldering -> active MM), adult
meta.population: Adults (median age at diagnosis ~69). The spectrum stays in one clinic: MGUS is monitored, high-risk smoldering myeloma is a randomized fork (AQUILA), active disease splits by transplant eligibility, and the relapse menu is routed by EXPOSURE - what the disease has already seen (lenalidomide, triple-class, BCMA) decides what can still work. AL amyloidosis is a DIFFERENT disease (same clone, organ emergency) - the AL gate reroutes it out.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the multi-line sequencing archetype - the disease with the deepest menu in oncology and the sharpest endpoint honesty problem: its newest standards (quadruplets, CAR-T) rank on progression-free survival because their overall survival is still maturing, its transplant question produced a PFS win with OS equivalence (DETERMINATION), and its regulatory history holds both an efficacy reversal (melflufen) and the first full withdrawal-and-return arc (belantamab).
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: IMWG updated diagnostic criteria (Rajkumar 2014): SLiM-CRAB biomarkers moved the treatment line into the former smoldering population
meta.response: IMWG response criteria incl. MRD; risk by R-ISS (ISS + high-risk cytogenetics + LDH)

stages.label: Presentation & activity boundary
stages.question: MGUS, smoldering, or active myeloma - where on the spectrum is this clone?
stages.decision: Apply SLiM-CRAB: end-organ damage OR a validated biomarker of inevitability (>=60% plasma cells, FLC ratio >=100, >1 focal MRI lesion) defines active disease.

stages.label: Risk & the AL check
stages.question: R-ISS risk group - and is any of this actually AL amyloidosis?
stages.decision: Cytogenetics (del(17p), t(4;14), t(14;16)), ISS labs, LDH -> R-ISS; screen for AL features (cardiac biomarkers, proteinuria) in every workup.

stages.label: Plan first-line therapy
stages.question: Smoldering: treat the precursor or monitor? Active: transplant-eligible or not?
stages.decision: High-risk SMM: the AQUILA fork (daratumumab vs active monitoring) is now a real randomized choice. Active TE: quadruplet induction era (PERSEUS). Active TI: da…

stages.label: MRD checkpoint
stages.question: MRD-negative after induction/consolidation - what does it change TODAY?
stages.decision: MRD calibrates the relapse posterior and the surveillance interval; de-escalation on MRD is a trial question, not a standard.

stages.label: Transplant fork
stages.question: Upfront ASCT, or induction alone with transplant banked?
stages.decision: DETERMINATION: upfront ASCT added 21 months of median PFS (67.5 vs 46.2) - and 5-year OS was 80.7% vs 79.2%. Both answers are defensible; the trainer shows bot…

stages.label: Relapse: exposure-routed sequencing
stages.question: What has the disease already seen - and what does that close or open?
stages.decision: Len-refractory + 1-3 lines opens CARTITUDE-4 territory (cilta-cel); triple-class exposure opens bispecifics; BCMA exposure routes toward GPRC5D; belantamab's r…

stages.label: Trial screen
stages.question: Which open randomized options exist for this profile?
stages.decision: Screen the live phase-3 menu: MajesTEC-4 (bispecific maintenance post-ASCT), linvoseltamab vs daratumumab in high-risk SMM (the post-AQUILA question), Magnetis…

stages.label: Decision artifacts
stages.question: Which results are load-bearing for this plan?
stages.decision: SLiM-CRAB panel (FLC ratio, marrow burden, MRI), cytogenetics/FISH, AL screen (NT-proBNP, urine), MRD assay, exposure ledger (the drugs the disease has seen).

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: Median age at diagnosis ~69. MAIA's update showed clinically meaningful benefit across age groups including >=80 - age modifies expectations, it does not close the modern menu.
Patient.helpPatient: Myeloma is mostly diagnosed in later life, and the modern treatments were tested in - and work for - older patients.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: Frailty shapes both the numbers and the menu - the guideline pathways split fit/intermediate/frail throughout.
Patient.helpPatient: How much daily life is limited. It steers dose and regimen choices more than it closes doors.

Patient.label: Transplant eligibility
Patient.help: A deliberate assessment (organ function, fitness), not an age cutoff. It forks the frontline menu: quadruplet+ASCT territory vs the MAIA pathway.
Patient.helpPatient: Whether high-dose therapy with your own stored stem cells is medically realistic. Both paths have strong modern options.

Disease.label: Spectrum position (IMWG)
Disease.help: SLiM-CRAB position. MGUS: monitor only - ranking is withheld because there is nothing to rank. High-risk SMM: the AQUILA fork. Active: the full menu.
Disease.helpPatient: Where on the spectrum this clone sits - from 'watch it once a year' to 'treat it now'. The line between them was drawn by evidence, and it moved in 2014 on purpose.

Disease.label: AL amyloidosis features
Disease.help: Light-chain organ deposition (cardiac biomarkers, nephrotic proteinuria, neuropathy) makes this AL amyloidosis - same clone, different disease, organ-directed playbook. Every MM trial cited here excl…
Disease.helpPatient: Sometimes the abnormal protein itself injures organs like the heart or kidneys. That is a different disease with its own plan - this trainer hands it off rather than guessing.

Disease.label: Cytogenetic risk (FISH)
Disease.help: The R-ISS high-risk lesions. Ranking waits for FISH: risk shades every arm's expectations and drives the maintenance/trial conversation.
Disease.helpPatient: A chromosome test on the myeloma cells. It is worth the wait - it changes how hard the plan pushes.

On treatment.label: MRD after induction/consolidation
On treatment.help: Myeloma's strongest surrogate - it recalibrates the relapse posterior and the follow-up interval. De-escalating therapy on MRD is a trial question, not a standard.
On treatment.helpPatient: The deepest measure of how little disease is left. Good news changes the forecast; it does not yet change the maintenance plan outside a study.

Relapse routing.label: Prior lines of therapy
Relapse routing.help: The line count is a routing key: CARTITUDE-4 enrolled 1-3 prior lines; talquetamab's label starts at >=4.
Relapse routing.helpPatient: How many treatment chapters are already written. Some options belong to early chapters, some to late ones.

Relapse routing.label: Lenalidomide-refractory
Relapse routing.help: Most first relapses now happen ON lenalidomide maintenance - the CARTITUDE-4 population. Refractoriness to the backbone is the modern relapse's defining fact.
Relapse routing.helpPatient: Whether the disease came back while the maintenance pill was still being taken. It usually did - and the menu is built for exactly that.

Relapse routing.label: Triple-class exposed
Relapse routing.help: Exposure to all three classic classes is the bispecific era's entry ticket - MajesTEC-1 enrolled exactly this population.
Relapse routing.helpPatient: Whether the three classic drug families have all been used. After that, the immune-redirecting options take over.

Relapse routing.label: Prior BCMA-directed therapy
Relapse routing.help: The target itself becomes an exposure: after BCMA CAR-T or a BCMA bispecific, the honest next move changes target (GPRC5D - talquetamab).
Relapse routing.helpPatient: These new treatments aim at a flag on the myeloma cell. Once one flag has been used, the next treatment often aims at a different flag.

Where you are.label: months since diagnosis
Where you are.help: Twin clock: places 'you are here' on the months-from-diagnosis axis. Not read by the engine (completeness_only).
Where you are.helpPatient: How long since your diagnosis - marks where you are on the modelled journey.

Where you are.label: Your state (optional)
Where you are.help: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.
Where you are.helpPatient: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.

Newly diagnosed.name: Daratumumab for high-risk smoldering (AQUILA)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN Myeloma v5.2026 (AQUILA-era option for high-risk SMM)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: modest: hypertension was the most common grade 3-4 event (5.7%); discontinuation for AEs 5.7%
Newly diagnosed.patient: Treating the precursor before it becomes myeloma: a shot that, in the deciding trial, cut progression risk in half and modestly improved survival at five years.

Newly diagnosed.name: Active monitoring for high-risk smoldering (the other AQUILA arm)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; the cost is measured in progression risk, not side effects
Newly diagnosed.patient: Watching carefully with treatment held in reserve - the same trial that tested early treatment also measured this path honestly, and both cards show their numbers.

Newly diagnosed.name: Dara-VRd quadruplet + ASCT (PERSEUS era)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN Myeloma v5.2026 (quadruplet era; Isa-VRd category 1 preferred alternative)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS primary met; OS immature
Newly diagnosed.patient: The modern four-drug induction plus transplant: the deepest remissions ever measured in this disease. Its card is honest that the survival ledger is still being written - that is what 'newest' means.

Newly diagnosed.name: VRd + upfront ASCT (DETERMINATION)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: grade >=3 treatment-related AEs 94.2% - the transplant block is the hardest stretch
Newly diagnosed.patient: The proven triplet with the transplant done upfront: almost two extra years before the disease moves again, in exchange for the hardest months early.

Newly diagnosed.name: VRd with ASCT banked (DETERMINATION delayed arm)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: grade >=3 treatment-related AEs 78.2% - meaningfully lighter than the upfront-transplant arm's 94.2%
Newly diagnosed.patient: Same drugs, transplant kept in the bank: at five years, survival was the same as doing it upfront. The cost is a shorter first remission; the benefit is deferring the hardest months - maybe indefinitely.

Newly diagnosed.name: Dara-Rd (MAIA, transplant-ineligible)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: manageable chronic-therapy profile; benefit held across age groups including >=80
Newly diagnosed.patient: The standard when transplant is off the table: a shot plus a pill, continued as long as it works - with mature five-year survival numbers behind it.

Newly diagnosed.name: Rd doublet (MAIA comparator)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN Myeloma v5.2026 (when anti-CD38 not feasible)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: lighter than the triplet; the price appears in the survival column instead
Newly diagnosed.patient: The pill-plus-steroid doublet: simpler and gentler, with honestly smaller numbers - its own trial is the reason the antibody is usually added.

Newly diagnosed.name: Supportive care only
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; the disease's bone pain and infections dominate - palliative care carries this path
Newly diagnosed.patient: Full attention on comfort without disease-directed treatment. In this disease that choice carries hard numbers, and the card shows them rather than hiding them.
drugs: Palliative care partnership; bone and transfusion support

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Cilta-cel CAR-T at first relapse (CARTITUDE-4)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS primary met; OS immature at primary
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: CRS 76.1% (grade 3-4 1.1%), ICANS 4.5%, cranial nerve palsy 9.1%, CAR-T neuropathy 2.8% - a specialized-center toxicity program is part of the prescription
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Your own T cells re-engineered against the myeloma, given once. At first relapse it beat standard care decisively on disease control - and then, for most, a treatment-free stretch.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Belantamab mafodotin + Vd (DREAMM-7 - the return)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN Myeloma v5.2026 category 1 (>=2 prior lines)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: ocular toxicity 92% (grade 3-4 77%; dose modification 83%) - the eye program is not a footnote, it is the arm's defining logistics
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A guided missile against the myeloma flag, back on the market after proving itself the second time - with survival numbers, and with eye side effects that shape the whole plan.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Dara-Vd triplet (DREAMM-7 comparator)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: familiar anti-CD38 + PI profile; no ocular program required
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The established relapse triplet - beaten in its head-to-head, still real and still right for some, without the eye-exam calendar.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Teclistamab bispecific (MajesTEC-1, triple-class exposed)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: CRS 72.1% (mostly low-grade), infections 76.4% (grade 3-4 44.8%), neutropenia 70.9% - the infection program is the long-game toxicity story
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: An off-the-shelf antibody that drafts your T cells against the myeloma - for disease that has seen all three classic drug families, most people respond.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Talquetamab - the target switch (GPRC5D)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN Myeloma v5.2026 (>=4 prior lines; the post-BCMA lane)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 1-2 registrational (accelerated approval - confirmatory trials ongoing)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: boxed warning CRS + neurologic toxicity; the signature is oral (dysgeusia, dry mouth) plus skin and nail changes - quality-of-life toxicities that deserve plai…
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: When the BCMA flag has been used, this one aims at a different flag - and most heavily pretreated patients respond. Its taste and skin side effects are real and worth naming out loud.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Pomalidomide-dexamethasone (conventional lane)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN Myeloma v5.2026 (backbone for many triplet builds)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 comparator arm (provenance: trade coverage - confirm)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: cytopenias, fatigue; a familiar, manageable profile
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The next pill in the same family after lenalidomide stops working - usually as the base a third drug is built onto.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: After many chapters, choosing comfort is a real chapter too - with the bone and blood support continued exactly as far as it serves you.
drugs: Palliative care partnership; bone, transfusion, and infection support per goals

honesty: Unverified statuses never carry the current date; every 'confirm' lives in the manifest staleness list.

PFS never impersonates OS: the two most modern cards on this menu (PERSEUS quadruplet, CARTITUDE-4 CAR-T) carry labeled PFS endpoints and DO NOT RANK, because their overall survival is immature - the newest standard ran…
The DETERMINATION pair renders both answers: upfront ASCT's 21-month PFS win AND the 5-year OS tie (80.7% vs 79.2%) - neither card is the lesser card; they are different bets about time and toxicity.

The melflufen story is kept as an efficacy-reversal teaching case, not an arm: its confirmatory trial showed SHORTER survival than the comparator this menu still carries (pom-dex, 25.0 months), and the approval was with…

The belantamab card carries the factory's first full withdrawal-AND-return reversal_note: withdrawn 2022 on a confirmatory miss, re-approved 2025-10-23 on DREAMM-7 - 'approved' is a claim with history, in both direction…
MGUS withholds ranking by design: the correct menu is empty, and teaching that inaction is a decision is the left edge of this spectrum.
Cross-trial comparison caveat: arms on one menu were earned in different trials with different populations; horizon chips are load-bearing.

Registry wins for status; the peer-reviewed paper wins for numbers; both are logged. The pom-dex 25.0-month anchor is trade-coverage provenance pending full-paper re-verification, and its card says so.
gates: Light-chain organ deposition = AL amyloidosis - same clone, different disease (organ-directed goals, own trials)
MGUS is monitored, never treated - there is nothing to rank
Cytogenetic risk (FISH) must be resulted before therapy ranking
care: FACT-accredited CAR-T program + CARVYKTI REMS (the logistics are the therapy)
Bispecific step-up capability + REMS, then community handoff

surveillance.cadence: MGUS: annual labs. High-risk SMM: q3-6 month labs + FLC, imaging on signal - or the AQUILA treatment fork
monthly M-protein and FLC; MRD at protocol landmarks; the exposure ledger updates with every line
